children: The euro remains vulnerable to renewed losses due to ongoing French fiscal risks, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. French government bond spreads remain wide with right-wing presidential candidate Marine Le Pen's promise to slash public spending raising more questions than it answered, he says. Barring a big U.S. policy misstep which questions investors' exposure to the dollar, the macro story remains negative for the euro, he says. The euro rises 0.1% to $1.1207 as oil prices ease after President Trump announced a Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire. The euro reached its lowest level in more than 16 months last week at $1.1160, according to LSEG, and ING sees the risk of it falling towards $1.110-$1.1120 in the near term. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
